title: Why Hot Grease Causes Solid Drain Blockages
description: Educational tip explaining how liquid fats, oils, and grease (FOG) cool and solidify inside kitchen drain lines, causing severe blockages.
image_prompt: A professional educational 3D cutaway illustration of a kitchen sink PVC drain pipe system in vertical 9:16 composition. The main focus is a detailed cross-section of a horizontal grey plastic waste pipe running under a sink cabinet. Inside the cutaway view of the pipe, a thick, realistic layer of solidified yellowish-white fat and grease coats the lower inner walls, narrowing the water passage. Clear, non-pressurized drainage water flows slowly over the buildup. Clean, realistic plumbing fittings including a P-trap and sanitary tee are correctly installed. Bright studio lighting illuminates the pipe interior. Clean composition with empty space at the top and bottom third for text overlays. Photorealistic textures, accurate pipe connections, no text, no logos, no watermarks, no labels, physically realistic geometry.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear pipe cutaway to reveal what happens hidden inside drain lines. Viewers notice how hot grease, which enters the sink as a liquid, coats the interior pipe walls as it cools down farther along the line. This visual reinforces why flushing hot grease with running water does not prevent long-term buildup in underground or concealed drain pipes.

on_image_text.hook: Hot liquid grease solidifies inside cold pipes.
on_image_text.explanation: As liquid fats travel into cooler drainage pipes, they solidify along the pipe walls and catch food scraps.
on_image_text.takeaway: Scrape grease into a container or trash before washing pans.
